technical.lead: Unsloth v0.1.47-beta adds GLM-5.2, Model Hub, 3x longer contexts
technical.body: The Unsloth fine-tuning stack tagged v0.1.47-beta on June 18, headlined by a new auto-fit context algorithm plus multi-token prediction that the project says roughly triples usable context in fixed memory: on a single 32GB GPU in f16 the maximum context grows from about 23,040 to 64,000 tokens without spilling, lowering the hardware bar for long-context fine-tuning on single-card setups. The build adds full GLM-5.2 support across all reasoning levels in Unsloth Studio, a redesigned full-page Model Hub with a trending feed and faster Xet downloads, a --secure Cloudflare-only mode, restored vLLM 0.22+ compatibility, DeepSeek-OCR vision, and better Blackwell handling. As a beta the figures are self-reported.

technical.lead: Liquid AI ships two 350M open-weight retrieval models for on-device search
technical.body: Liquid AI published two small open-weight retrieval models on June 19 under its LFM Open License v1.0: LFM2.5-Embedding-350M, a dense bi-encoder that maps a document to one vector, and LFM2.5-ColBERT-350M, a late-interaction model producing per-token vectors for finer matching. Both are 350M parameters, derived from a shared backbone by swapping causal for bidirectional attention, and cover 11 languages. The ColBERT variant is reported at 0.605 NDCG@10 on NanoBEIR and 0.694 Recall@20 on MKQA-11, with GGUF builds running under llama.cpp at median query latency below 10 ms on a MacBook Pro M4 Max, making it the kind of fast, permissively licensed component that lets local LLM stacks do grounded RAG without a server-side embedding call. Numbers are self-reported and await third-party reproduction.

citations.label: MarkTechPost - Liquid AI introduces LFM2.5-Embedding-350M and LFM2.5-ColBERT-350M

technical.lead: Coding-agent harnesses add control and record-once features
technical.body: Three state-changes landed across the coding-agent space on June 18-20. Nous Research added a Blank Slate setup mode to its open-source Hermes Agent framework: an agent boots with only a provider/model, File Operations and Terminal toolsets, while web, browser, code execution, vision, memory, delegation, cron, skills, plugins and MCP stay off until explicitly enabled and pinned durably to disk, a least-privilege attack-surface posture. The same day OpenAI shipped Record & Replay for its Codex macOS app (build 26.616), where a user walks the agent through a desktop workflow once and it is captured as a reusable skill to re-run unattended. And Cisco open-sourced FAPO, a Claude-Code-driven prompt optimizer that evaluates whole multi-step pipelines, attributes failures to a specific stage, and reports a +14.1-point mean gain over GEPA across 15 of 18 model-benchmark pairs.

technical.lead: NVIDIA's training-free SpatialClaw tops 20 spatial-reasoning benchmarks
technical.body: NVIDIA researchers released SpatialClaw on June 19, a training-free framework that gives vision-language models a way to reason about object localization and 3D relationships without any model- or benchmark-specific tuning. Instead of retraining, it wraps a stateful Python kernel pre-loaded with the input frames and perception primitives, and the agent writes one Python cell per step into that persistent kernel, enabling genuine test-time computation such as switching from a centroid-distance heuristic to a KD-tree nearest-neighbor search mid-task. The reported results put code-as-action ahead of prior tool-use approaches: 59.9% average accuracy across 20 spatial benchmarks, +11.2 points over the SpaceTools baseline, with the largest gains on dynamic tasks and consistency across six backbones from 26B to 397B parameters. Code is open on GitHub (NVlabs/SpatialClaw) with a project page and paper, making it a reproducible applied result.

citations.label: MarkTechPost - NVIDIA introduces SpatialClaw, a training-free agent that treats code as the action interface for spatial reasoning

technical.lead: AI events ahead: confidential computing, offensive security, World's Fair
technical.body: The forward calendar across three sub-tracks, with the soonest events now days out and nothing yet past its end date. Mainstream dev/data: Snowflake runs a virtual Dev Day on June 25; the AI Engineer World's Fair takes over Moscone West June 29 through July 2 (optional New Engineer Orientation June 28), billed as the largest technical AI-engineering conference with over 20 tracks, around 250 speakers, dedicated Inference and Security tracks, and OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Amazon AGI Labs and Microsoft attending, preceded by the official hackathon with Cerebral Valley June 27-28; further out, GitHub Universe returns October 28-29 and AWS re:Invent runs November 30 through December 4. AI-security: the Confidential Computing Summit lands June 23-24 at the San Francisco Mint (Linux Foundation and OPAQUE); AI Tinkerers SF hosts an Offensive Security Demo Night on June 25 (sponsor XBOW); SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit follows August 11-12; Black Hat USA's AI Summit runs August 1-6; and OWASP Global AppSec USA is November 5-6. AI-chip/hardware: AMD's Advancing AI 2026 is July 23 at Moscone, Hot Chips 2026 runs August 23-25 at Stanford, and the AI Infra Summit is September 15-17 in Santa Clara.
